name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-MIL 'Garrison'
description:
The KP-MIL 'Garrison' is Kang-Petrov's military and law-enforcement contract variant — a KP-19 platform reworked to ADS (Arcturus Defense Solutions) service specifications. The frame is manufactured from a higher-grade polymer compound with a matte olive-gray finish instead of the standard Slagworks-recycled black, and the slide is salt-bath nitrided rather than phosphated, giving it a significantly harder and more corrosion-resistant surface that maintains finish integrity in the perpetual damp of GLMZ's lake-effect climate. The trigger group is upgraded to a 2.6kg flat-face unit with a shorter reset, the front sight is a tritium-inlaid unit for low-light use, and the frame comes standard with an extended beaver-tail grip that reduces the chance of slide bite on high-grip operators. Chambered in 9x19mm Caseless as the standard ADS service round, with a 17-round magazine. Surplus and black-market examples chambered in Standard brass also circulate.

The KP-MIL is not sold to civilians. It is issued to Arcturus Civil Security contract personnel, certain Slagworks corporate security tiers, and under the ADS service contract, to whatever paramilitary forces Arcturus has deployed in the current quarter. This makes civilian possession inherently a story — every KP-MIL in private hands was either stolen, bought from a corrupt issuing officer, or recovered from a body. The olive-gray frame is immediately recognizable on the street, and carrying one without a visible ACS credential is the kind of decision that tends to start conversations with the wrong people.

The 'Garrison' nickname comes from its official ADS designation in the service contract language, not from any street tradition — but the name stuck because it fits. The gun looks like something issued, not purchased. It has the slightly impersonal quality of equipment that was never meant to be owned, only used. Operators who acquire them illegally sometimes strip the finish or dye the frame black specifically to obscure the origin.
specifications: caliber: 9x19mm Caseless effective_range: 55m rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic magazine_capacity: 17 rounds weight: 0.74 kg
tactical_use: The KP-MIL performs identically to the KP-19CL in most operational contexts with the added benefit of the nitrided slide's improved durability in wet conditions and the tritium sight's utility in GLMZ's frequent low-light environments. ACS operators run it as a primary sidearm for patrol roles where a full-size pistol is appropriate. The improved trigger and beaver-tail make it more forgiving of inconsistent grip technique, which matters for a service weapon issued to personnel with widely varying levels of training. The caseless chambering is standard ACS protocol for indoor operations.
cultural_context: In GLMZ, the olive-gray KP-MIL frame is a social signal of considerable power. Carried openly with ACS credentials, it commands a specific deference in contested zones — the gun of the people with official sanction to use force. Carried covertly without credentials, it implies a level of access to restricted supply chains that makes most people nervous. Black-market KP-MIL pistols command a 300% premium over retail KP-19 pricing specifically because of what the frame color communicates to observers who recognize it.
known_users: black-market operators with ACS supply chain access
former ACS personnel who retained their service weapon
story_hooks: Kyle Corbin-Vasik recovers a KP-MIL from a scene where the dead ACS officer's serial number traces back to a unit that was officially listed as destroyed in an armory fire two years ago — along with forty-seven other KP-MILs that are apparently now somewhere in GLMZ.

An Excluded encampment leader is carrying a KP-MIL openly — olive-gray frame, tritium sights, ACS-issue mag — and when asked where she got it, she just says 'it was left for me' and won't say anything more.
